I had completely forgotten I wrote mispelr. It surfaced while I was working on
, which uses it to misspell poems, and there it was, a browser toy from 2015 that takes perfectly good text and ruins it.
The mispelr playground: input text, six method buttons, a chance slider set to 50%, and the respelled output with changed words highlighted
It has six ways to do the ruining:
swaps in real-world misspellings from a dictionary of common typos
transposes two adjacent letters, never the first ("Teh qucik bronw fxo")
mixes the others, word by word

It did what I wanted, but I was never completely happy with it. Every word went through the respeller once, and some came back unchanged, but how much of a sentence got mangled depended on the method and the dice and it was usually too much. There was no way to set it. And TBH, it was more annoying than anything else. Which was disappointing, since it did what I wanted. But eating a gallon of ice-cream in one go is not fun.
So I brought it back up to speed. It lives in
now, next to PoeticalBot. It's on npm as

Extending the README also turned up a bug that had been sitting in the data for eleven years. A few rows in the homophone list were written as prose -
- and the conversion script kept the "and". So
turned "their" into "and they're". I'd seen it in the playground but not chased it. Generating examples from real seeded output put it right in front of me. Fixed in 0.1.1.
